newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan bank expects two bln rupee profit in '97.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan bank expects two bln rupee profit in '97.

text.p: Pakistan's Muslim Commercial Bank (MCB) said on Wednesday it was likely to make a pre-tax profit of two billion rupees in calendar 1997, compared to 268 million in 1996.
"The profit will rise due to reorganisation and recovery of loans," MCB president Mohammad Mansha told a news briefing briefing.
He said the profit of the bank, which was privatised in 1991, had falled in 1996 owing to political and economic uncertainties after a pre-tax profit of 928 million in 1995.
The MCB, whose 10-rupee stock rose 2.00 to 33.25 on Wednesday, is now concentrating on banking business rather than property, equities and commodities businesses, Mansha said.

He said the bank had curtailed financing edible oil imports because of alleged irregularities in that business, but would continue gold import, which which was worth $282 million in the past two years, making it Pakistan's largest gold importer.
In the first quarter of 1997, the bank's pre-tax profit rose to 452 million rupees compared to 237 million in the same period of the previous year, Mansha said.
